introduction.objective: Find how much space a block fills by counting its equal cubes in layers.
introduction.successCriteria: On a block you have not seen, say how many cubes are in one layer, how many layers there are and how many cubes altogether, and explain how that counts every cube once.

learningGoals.objective: Count a block of equal cubes as equal layers.

lookFor: A checked plan on a fresh block where cubes in one layer, number of layers and cubes altogether all match the block, with assisted false.
Own words that join the three, for example "six on the bottom, and there are three of those, so eighteen". Adding the layers and multiplying are both right.
notEnough: A right total with a wrong layer count, or a right layer count with a wrong total.
A plan checked after the layers were opened, after an explanation was shown on that block, after resume_activity reopened it, or after the counts were said aloud: its event carries assisted true.
Agreeing with an explanation, or repeating a count the tutor just gave.
Placing and stacking cubes in the building activity: it shows what a layer is, not that the child can count with one.
Counting the squares on the outside faces, or only the cubes that can be seen.

skills.description: Count all the cubes in one layer
skills.prompt: How do you feel about counting all the cubes in one layer on your own?

skills.description: Use layers to count a whole block
skills.prompt: How do you feel about using layers to work out how many cubes are in a whole block?

observationPrompt: Look at the latest event. layer_stacked or back_rows_added: the child changed the block while building, so anything said about the old count is out of date; use the new counts in the event and state, and ask what they notice rather than telling them the total. response_committed: the child checked a plan. Read view.screen.checkedPlan: the three numbers they entered, the block’s real counts and wrongFields; the attempt carries the assisted flag. If a number is wrong, work on that number only: show_moment layer_help for cubes in one layer, repetition_help for the total, then resume_activity so they can put it right in the same boxes (that retry is recorded as assisted). If all three are right, say so and do not ask for the same counts again; if you do not yet know how they found it, ask. A right plan with assisted true is practice, not a fresh check.
tutorGuidance:
Use this map adaptively; it is a set of opportunities, not an order. The block on the table is real to the model: view.screen.counts gives the exact numbers (perLayer, layers, total), so never count from memory. show_moment speaks a short explanation in the lesson’s own words while the block shows it, then hands back to you in the same turn: follow it with one small thing for the child to count, predict or explain. Most moments highlight the block in hand and leave the child in control of it. The child can turn the block and open or close its layers at any time.
1. ONE CUBE IS ONE. Worth showing when the child counts faces or squares, or counts a corner cube twice: unit_help colours one cube. Evidence: says the coloured piece is one cube although three faces show. Not evidence: agreeing.
2. A LAYER IS ONE FLAT LEVEL, BACK ROWS INCLUDED. one_layer colours the bottom layer and gives its count; layer_example brings a small two-layer block. The child can build one: start_activity build_layer gives an empty 3 by 2 layer to fill cube by cube, then Stack layer and Add back rows. Evidence: counts a whole layer, back row included, without being told the number. Building alone shows what a layer is, not that they can count with it.
3. EQUAL LAYERS MAKE THE BLOCK. layers opens the block and gives cubes in one layer, layers and total; repetition_help is for a right layer count with a wrong total. Opening layers never adds cubes: the child can use Open layers or drag up to see this, and start_activity explore_block gives a 3 by 3 by 3 block to look round freely. Evidence: own words joining one layer, how many layers and the total; adding and multiplying are both right.
4. A PLAN ON A FRESH BLOCK. start_check layer_plan gives a closed block the child has not seen and three boxes to fill before pressing Check my plan; the lesson speaks the question. Situation small is the first step (the very first is 2 by 2 by 2); large and long change the size, the shape and the arithmetic. Do not say the counts, open the layers or show a moment on that block first unless the child asks for help: each makes the attempt assisted. Evidence: all three numbers right with assisted false, ideally with how they found it. A child who already explains layers at the start can go straight here.
A MISTAKE TO WATCH FOR, NOT A TOPIC. Some children count only the cubes they can see, or count the squares on the faces, and so leave out cubes at the back or in the middle. Counting in layers already prevents this, so most children never need it mentioned. Do not ask about hidden cubes, do not go looking for them, and do not present them as something special. Raise it only when the child’s own count or words show the mistake, or they ask: then inside (refused unless the block has a cube shut in on every side) or larger_example shows that the cube in the middle is just part of the middle layer, and no_buried agrees with a child who says a thin block has none. Once is enough; go back to layers.
HELP ON CURRENT WORK. After a checked plan, compare_plan sets their numbers beside the opened block; then resume_activity reopens the same boxes for them to correct, recorded as assisted. set_layers opens or closes the layers when the child only asks for that; opening before a plan is checked marks it assisted. layer_example and larger_example replace the block, so they are refused while a plan is unchecked: talk about leaving the plan first (leave_activity).
SPOKEN ANSWERS. If the child says all three numbers for a waiting plan, call answer_check with its sceneId, values (cubes in one layer, number of layers, cubes altogether, in that order, as digits) and their words. If they say only one or two, ask for the rest or let them type; never fill in a number they did not say.
WHAT THE MODEL RECORDS. Each checked plan is a response_committed event with what was entered, correct and assisted. Numbers typed but not checked, and earlier attempts, are not the current answer. If start_check is refused because no unused blocks are left in that situation, try another situation or carry on with the examples, and do not call that work a fresh check.
FACTS TO KEEP RIGHT. Volume here is how much space the block fills, measured by counting equal cubes with no gaps. Turning the block or pulling the layers apart does not change the number of cubes. Dimensions are width, rows back and layers high; any way of slicing into equal layers would count the same total, but this model only opens horizontal layers.
LIMITS OF THIS MODEL. The cubes have no real size, so do not give centimetres. The thin lines between cubes are drawn edges, not gaps. You know the exact counts but not what the child can see from their angle. A plan with three labelled boxes hands the child the method: it does not show they would choose layers unprompted.
WORDS. Say cubes, layer, altogether, the back row. Keep volume for when it is explained, and keep factors, horizontal and independent out of what the child hears.
